items.title: Sightlines Issue No.3: Raise the bar for how teams use AI
items.excerpt: Figma's Sightlines newsletter on driving AI adoption across product teams and making better decisions about what to build with AI.
items.note: Adjacent to 10-11 Figma rituals story; distinct issue.

items.title: Tesler's Law: complexity moved to a different part of the journey
items.excerpt: AI did not remove the complexity of software; it removed the interface that told you where the complexity went. Applies Tesler's Law of conservation of complexity to chat-field AI products.
items.note: Date from outlet RSS pubDate (Medium is Cloudflare-blocked for curl/WebFetch).

items.title: AI-generated UI is fast design, not UX
items.excerpt: An editor's pick arguing that AI-generated interfaces speed up production but skip problem discovery, and making the case for wandering and craft in the age of AI.
items.note: Date from outlet RSS pubDate (Medium Cloudflare-blocked). Within window by ~1h17m.

items.title: What the AI era owes you
items.excerpt: No one is going to save your design career from AI, the author argues; like the 1820 handloom weaver, designers need to build a version of themselves the next economy will need.
items.note: Date from outlet RSS pubDate. Career essay, weaker news hook.

items.title: Why 'boring' AI is Hollywood's best bet
items.excerpt: Generative AI could be the film industry's secret weapon, but not in the way people expect: the real wins are in unglamorous production and VFX pipeline tasks.

items.title: Nikon microscopic video competition winner disqualified for using generative AI
items.excerpt: Nikon is revisiting its Small World in Motion competition rules after the original winning video turned out to be made with generative AI.

items.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
items.excerpt: A hands-on account of running local models (Hermes, Qwen) on a Mac Studio and laptop: what works, what breaks, and why doing AI on your own terms is still hard.
items.note: Matches rotation emphasis Ollama/local LLM; designer hook is indirect.

items.title: Figma to Claude Code: What we learned after using it
items.excerpt: A design agency's field report on the Figma-to-Claude Code workflow: real use cases, where the round trip between frames and code works, and its limitations.
items.note: JSON-LD datePublished Oct 09 2026; the identical 14:46:06 timestamp appears on other Eleken posts, so this may be a CMS republish. Verify before picking.

items.title: Inside Vibe Design: An agency's field guide to designing with AI in 2026
items.excerpt: How AI is changing UX/UI practice at a product design agency: the vibe-design workflow, the tools in use, and where human judgment still matters.
items.note: Same CMS bulk-timestamp caveat as the other Eleken post.

items.title: Will 'boring' robots win in the real world? Why robotic form should follow workflow
items.excerpt: Humanoid makers are adding wheels and manipulators and dropping heads and eyes. The piece argues that physical AI product design should start from the workflow, not from robot-forward spectacle.
items.note: Off-list (therobotreport.com); industrial-design angle on embodied AI. Hero image is Atlas (de-emphasized topic).

items.excerpt: Artec Twins combines point clouds, meshes and Gaussian Splats in one platform for processing, rendering and measuring digital twins with billions of points.

items.title: Odyssey-3 is a new generative world model that you can try for free

items.title: Context Libraries: How AI power users manage context engineering
items.excerpt: NN/g research finds Claude power users rarely edit their context files and often can't find them. Your AI agent is only as powerful as its context library.
